parameters.query:
-- Claim companies that are worth a contact lookup, and open the run in the same
-- statement so the agent_runs row is the claim (the pattern WF-04 uses).
--
-- docs/workflows.md: "Only enrich companies that already scored above the
-- threshold." That was written when enrichment cost provider credits. It costs
-- nothing now, but the rule stays: a contact for a company nobody will write to
-- is personal data held for no reason, which docs/security.md calls out under
-- data minimisation.
--
-- "No contact found is a normal outcome. The company stays scored and is not
-- retried for 30 days." The agent_runs row is that memory - there is no retry
-- column and no migration for one.
--
-- The per-domain fetch throttle from 0012 applies here too: WF-02 and WF-03 both
-- fetch from the same hosts, and the limit is per domain, not per workflow.
WITH candidates AS (
    SELECT c.id, c.domain
    FROM companies c
    WHERE c.status = 'scored'
      AND c.score_band IN ('OUTREACH', 'HIGH_PRIORITY', 'HOT')
      -- Someone contactable already exists: nothing to do.
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM people p
          WHERE p.company_id = c.id
            AND p.email IS NOT NULL
            AND p.email_status IN ('valid', 'catch_all', 'guessed')
      )
      -- Tried recently, found nothing. Not again yet.
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM agent_runs r
          WHERE r.company_id = c.id
            AND r.agent_name = 'enrichment'
            AND r.status IN ('success', 'skipped')
            AND r.started_at > now() - make_interval(days => ($1::jsonb ->> 'retry_days')::int)
      )
      -- Already being enriched by a run that is still alive.
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM agent_runs r
          WHERE r.company_id = c.id
            AND r.agent_name = 'enrichment'
            AND r.status     = 'running'
            AND r.started_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'
      )
    ORDER BY c.total_score DESC, c.updated_at
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'candidate_pool')::int
    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
allowed AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM candidates
    WHERE claim_domain_fetch(
              domain,
              make_interval(mins => ($1::jsonb ->> 'domain_cooldown_minutes')::int)
          )
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
),
claimed AS (
    UPDATE companies
    SET status = 'enriching'
    WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM allowed)
      AND status = 'scored'
    RETURNING id, name, domain, website
),
opened AS (
    INSERT INTO agent_runs (agent_name, company_id, input, status, model, started_at)
    SELECT 'enrichment', claimed.id, $1::jsonb -> 'input', 'running', $1::jsonb ->> 'model', now()
    FROM claimed
    RETURNING id AS agent_run_id, company_id
)
SELECT o.agent_run_id,
       c.id            AS company_id,
       c.name,
       c.domain::text  AS domain,
       c.website
FROM opened o
JOIN companies c ON c.id = o.company_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ batch_size: Number($env.ENRICH_BATCH_SIZE || 3), candidate_pool: Number($env.ENRICH_CANDIDATE_POOL || 15), retry_days: Number($env.ENRICH_RETRY_DAYS || 30), domain_cooldown_minutes: Number($env.RESEARCH_DOMAIN_COOLDOWN_MINUTES || 60), model: $env.OLLAMA_ENRICHMENT_MODEL || $env.OLLAMA_MODEL || 'llama3.1:8b', input: { execution_id: String($execution.id), workflow_id: $workflow.id, stage: 'enrichment' } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Write the verified contacts and hand the company back to scoring.
--
-- The company goes to 'researched', not to the 'ready' that docs/workflows.md
-- specifies. 'ready' is a dead end: WF-04 claims 'researched', and it is WF-04
-- that turns a person into a lead, so a company parked at 'ready' would have a
-- contact and never a lead. Back to 'researched' means the 15 minute scoring
-- pass picks it up, re-scores decision_maker from the people table, and creates
-- the lead. Finding nothing returns it to 'scored' untouched.
WITH payload AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p),
cand AS (
    SELECT (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid            AS company_id,
           person ->> 'full_name'                         AS full_name,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'first_name', '')            AS first_name,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'last_name', '')             AS last_name,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'title', '')                 AS title,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'seniority', '')             AS seniority,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'email', '')::citext         AS email,
           person ->> 'email_status'                      AS email_status,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'linkedin_url', '')          AS linkedin_url,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'source_url', '')            AS source_url,
           NULLIF(person ->> 'discovery_method', '')      AS discovery_method
    FROM payload, jsonb_array_elements(payload.p -> 'people') AS person
),
-- people has a unique index on email. An address that already belongs to a
-- different row would abort the whole insert, so it is dropped to NULL instead:
-- the person is still worth recording, and the row that already has the address
-- is the one that keeps it.
safe AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           existing.email        AS existing_email,
           existing.email_status AS existing_status,
           existing.source_url   AS existing_source,
           existing.discovery_method AS existing_method,
           CASE
               WHEN c.email IS NULL THEN NULL
               WHEN EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1 FROM people px
                   WHERE px.email = c.email
                     AND NOT (px.company_id = c.company_id
                              AND lower(btrim(px.full_name)) = lower(btrim(c.full_name)))
               ) THEN NULL
               ELSE c.email
           END AS incoming_email
    FROM cand c
    LEFT JOIN people existing
           ON existing.company_id = c.company_id
          AND lower(btrim(existing.full_name)) = lower(btrim(c.full_name))
),
-- Whether to take the incoming address is ONE decision, and the address, its
-- status, its source and how it was found all follow from it. Deciding each of
-- those separately is how a published address kept its status but picked up
-- discovery_method = 'pattern_inferred' on a re-run, which made the audit trail
-- say the opposite of the truth.
resolved AS (
    SELECT s.*,
           (s.incoming_email IS NOT NULL
            AND (s.existing_email IS NULL
                 OR s.existing_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'valid'
                 OR s.email_status = 'valid')) AS take_incoming
    FROM safe s
),
ins AS (
    INSERT INTO people (
        company_id, full_name, first_name, last_name, title, seniority,
        email, email_status, linkedin_url, source_url, discovery_method
    )
    SELECT company_id, full_name, first_name, last_name, title, seniority,
           CASE WHEN take_incoming THEN incoming_email ELSE existing_email END,
           CASE WHEN take_incoming THEN email_status
                ELSE COALESCE(existing_status, 'unknown') END,
           linkedin_url,
           COALESCE(CASE WHEN take_incoming THEN source_url ELSE existing_source END, source_url),
           CASE WHEN take_incoming THEN discovery_method ELSE existing_method END
    FROM resolved
    -- EXCLUDED already carries the resolved values, because the decision above
    -- was made against the row that is being conflicted with.
    ON CONFLICT (company_id, lower(btrim(full_name))) DO UPDATE
        SET title            = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.title, people.title),
            seniority        = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.seniority, people.seniority),
            linkedin_url     = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.linkedin_url, people.linkedin_url),
            email            = EXCLUDED.email,
            email_status     = EXCLUDED.email_status,
            source_url       = EXCLUDED.source_url,
            discovery_method = EXCLUDED.discovery_method
    RETURNING id, email, email_status
),
contactable AS (
    SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM ins WHERE email IS NOT NULL
),
upd AS (
    UPDATE companies
    SET status = CASE WHEN (SELECT n FROM contactable) > 0 THEN 'researched' ELSE 'scored' END
    WHERE id = (SELECT company_id FROM cand LIMIT 1)
      AND status = 'enriching'
    RETURNING id, status
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM ins)::int   AS people_written,
       (SELECT n FROM contactable)       AS contactable_written,
       (SELECT status FROM upd)          AS company_status,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id'      AS agent_run_id;

parameters.query:
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status        = 'success',
    output        = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    error         = NULL,
    prompt_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,prompt_tokens}')::int,
    output_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,completion_tokens}')::int,
    finished_at   = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, duration_ms;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ agent_run_id: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.agent_run_id, usage: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.usage, output: { people: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.people, role_addresses: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.role_addresses, dropped: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.dropped, notes: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.notes, pattern: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.pattern, derived_count: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.derived_count, sources: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.sources, people_written: $json.people_written, contactable_written: $json.contactable_written, model_output: $('Validate And Verify').item.json.model_output } } ) }}

nodes.notes: dropped is kept: what the model invented is as informative as what it read.

nodes.name: Enriched
nodes.notes: A run that found people. company_status should read 'researched'.

parameters.query:
-- Nothing usable came back. Put the company back exactly where it was and let
-- the 30 day window in the claim query keep it there.
--
-- The run is closed as 'error' only when the model itself failed. A company
-- whose pages simply do not name anybody is a 'skipped' run: it is not a fault,
-- and recording it as one would make the WF-101 error rate meaningless.
WITH payload AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p),
upd AS (
    UPDATE companies
    SET status = 'scored'
    FROM payload
    WHERE companies.id = (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid
      AND companies.status = 'enriching'
    RETURNING companies.id
),
run AS (
    UPDATE agent_runs
    SET status      = payload.p ->> 'run_status',
        error       = CASE WHEN payload.p ->> 'run_status' = 'error'
                           THEN COALESCE(NULLIF(payload.p ->> 'error', ''), 'Enrichment failed with no message')
                           ELSE NULL END,
        output      = payload.p -> 'output',
        finished_at = now()
    FROM payload
    WHERE agent_runs.id = (payload.p ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
    RETURNING agent_runs.id, agent_runs.status
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM upd)::int AS companies_released,
       (SELECT status FROM run)        AS run_status,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_id'      AS company_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ company_id: $json.company_id, agent_run_id: $json.agent_run_id, run_status: $json.run_status, error: $json.error_message, output: { people: $json.people, role_addresses: $json.role_addresses, dropped: $json.dropped, notes: $json.notes, errors: $json.errors, pages_fetched: $json.pages_fetched, raw_response: $json.raw_response } } ) }}
